findings.issue: “Both directions always occur” is too absolute. A reversible reaction can initially have zero reverse rate if no products are present. The relevant distinction is that both directions occurring does not establish equal rates.
findings.evidence: The sources require equal forward and reverse rates at equilibrium; they do not say both rates are always nonzero. The initial-zero-product counterexample is standard chemistry, judged independently of the supplied sources.

findings.issue: The Q < K row gives the direction backward. It should say “Reactants consumed, products formed.” It also contradicts the draft’s Full-credit answer.
findings.evidence: The CED explicitly states Q < K means net forward change toward products; Q > K means net reverse change toward reactants.

findings.issue: “More AgCl dissolves until Q = K” needs the condition that enough solid remains. An insufficient amount of AgCl can dissolve completely while the solution remains unsaturated, with Q < Ksp.
findings.evidence: This added dissolution scenario is judged as standard chemistry. Q < Ksp favors dissolution when solid is available, but saturation is not guaranteed if the solid is exhausted. Revise to “More AgCl dissolves; if sufficient solid is available, dissolution continues until Q = Ksp.”
